All evidence gathered (2 reference screenshots, 4 QA screenshots, PRODUCT.md, DESIGN.md, spec search sections, App.vue, search.ts, useMailbox.ts, style.css, InboxList.vue, ContactPane.vue). Findings below.

---

# 1. SUPERHUMAN BREAKDOWN

## Screenshot 1 — search overlay (empty query)
- **Full-screen dark overlay** over the dimmed app; the left icon rail (sparkle/AI, mail, calendar glyphs) stays visible at the far left. The overlay owns the whole viewport except the rail.
- **Header row of the overlay column:** "Search" label left, **X close** at the right edge of the input column.
- **Main column, two stacked groups separated by a hairline:**
  - *Contact suggestions* — 6 rows, two-column: display name (left, white, medium weight) + email (right, gray, mono-ish): "Sam Baillie / sam.baillie@globallogic.com", "Wispr Flow", "Charlie Williams", "Barclays", "DeepLearning.AI", "Whittard of Chelsea".
  - *Recent queries* — plain text rows: `from:mistura_yakubu@hotmail.co.uk`, "orbital", "deepseek", "whoop", "eta", "qwen", "canada", "berlioz", and **"kranbrothers" carrying a full-width gray selection bar** = the keyboard-selected suggestion (arrow-key highlight, no accent color).
- **Right-hand "Tips" column:** heading "Tips", then ~17 operator rows, each **operator (light, mono) on one line + plain-English gloss (gray, smaller) on the next**: `from:nicole`/"from Nicole", `to:roman`/"to Roman", `"be brilliant"`/'contains "be brilliant"', `has:attachment`/"with attachments", `subject:lunch`/'subject contains "lunch"', `in:sent`, `in:inbox`, `-in:inbox`/"not in the Inbox", `in:fundraising`/"in this label", `is:unread`, `is:starred`, `is:shared`, `before:2017/06/01`/"before June 2017", `after:2017/06/01`, `older_than:3d`/"more than 3 days ago", `newer_than:1m`/"1 month ago or later".
- **Bottom-right footer:** "Create Team" label + row of small icons.
- **Density/type:** near-black plane, ~13–14px UI type, generous row pitch, no dividers between suggestion rows except the one above recent queries, no cards, no shadows.

## Screenshot 2 — search results
- Same overlay persists; the browser chrome title reads "Search: sam.baillie@globallogic.com". **The query is now the list header** (16px white text) with the **X** at the right of that header row — query-as-header communicates "these results are *about* this query; X clears/closes; the query is the context, not a form you must re-read."
- **Sender-grouped results:** left column = sender name + **"(count)"** ("Sam Baillie (2)", "GLUKI-SMB-Hu… (7)", "Andrew, Sam (7)"); each sender cell can carry a hover highlight (yellow on "Sam Baillie"). Rows under a sender: **label chip** ("globallogic" purple chip, "career" red chip), **bold subject + gray snippet** on one line, **purple checkmark** (read/confirmed state), paperclip glyph, and a right-aligned **date** ("8/1/2024").
- **Selected row:** full-width dark-gray fill + **3–4px purple bar on the left edge** — identical "you are here" language to our focused row.
- **Attachment chips:** under affected rows, rounded chips with a red "PDF" tag + truncated filename ("Bebert_Sofiane_GL Of…", "First Advantage Candi…", "test-report-Sofiane-B…", "Senior Python Develo…").
- **Right contact card:** "GLUKI-SMB-Human Resourcing" (name wraps), "GLUKI-HR@globallogic.com", link glyph + "globallogic.com" — the searched correspondent's card, mirroring our ContactPane role.
- Rows are compact single lines; grouping compresses 18 results into ~6 sender blocks.

## Scope we intentionally do NOT copy (PRODUCT.md anti-reference "Superhuman feature-parity clone"; spec `U` items)
- The **full operator grammar** (labels `in:`, `is:unread/starred/shared`, `before:/after:/older_than:/newer_than:`, `has:attachment`, `in:sent`) — our grammar is deliberately text/from/to/subject + quotes + AND/OR/−; importing more operators is product scope, not look.
- **Read-receipt checkmarks** — spec explicitly separates recipient read-receipts from local read state; our gutter dot + "Mark read/unread" is the correct scope.
- Contact-card enrichment (domain link, fabricated profile data), "Create Team" footer, the AI sparkle glyph, multi-account/cross-account search, autocomplete ranking claims (spec marks ranking/hit-highlighting `U`/unverified), calendar.
## Visual/interaction reference we SHOULD match
Overlay density and dark plane; query-as-header with X; two-column operator+gloss Tips (adapted to *our supported* operators); suggestion rows (contacts + recent queries) with keyboard highlight; sender grouping with (count); chips for labels/attachments *when the data exists*; purple selection bar; right contact card; J/K through results with query preserved; Back restores the same results.

# 2. SIDE-BY-SIDE

| Superhuman element/behavior | Our equivalent | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Overlay search input, `/` to open, focus on open | In-flow form above list (`App.vue:1900`, `.mail-search`), `/` at `App.vue:1459`, header glyph `:1783`, focus moved to `#mail-query` in `revealSearch` (`App.vue:678-684`) | **Justified divergence** (Principle 3, "reuse established surfaces") — keyboard parity achieved; overlay would be closer visually |
| Contact suggestions + recent queries under input, keyboard-highlighted | **None** | **Real gap** (spec leaves autocomplete `U`, but recent queries are honest local data) |
| Tips: operator + plain-English gloss, two-column, scannable | One dense prose paragraph `#search-help` (`App.vue:1908`): "Use from:, to:, subject:, straight-quoted phrases, AND, OR, or -exclusions. AND binds before OR. Dates, labels, Cc/Bcc and parentheses are not supported." | **Real gap** — recognition vs recall |
| X to close/clear; query as results header | Editable input persists above results + "Back to previous context" button (`:1905`); Esc in input (`:1903`) hides form **and** exits search context; native `type=search` clear is unstyled | **Justified divergence** (spec: "Keep query editable") but missing visible clear/echo; Esc semantics too aggressive |
| Query-as-list-header | Query lives only in the editable input; results area has coverage line, no query echo | **Partial** — justified, but add compact query echo |
| Sender grouping with (count) | Flat list, date-group captions ("JANUARY 2025"), 132px sender column (`InboxList.vue:574`) | **Justified divergence** (spec: reuse conversation rows); grouping would aid `from:` queries — P3 |
| Label chips (globallogic/career) | None; `label:` unsupported by grammar (`search.ts`); an "Archive" chip appears in QA capture but not in current `InboxList.vue` source | **Justified** — out of scope; capture/code mismatch to verify |
| PDF attachment chips in rows | None; DESIGN.md §5 *promises* "an attachment glyph sits before the date when present" but `InboxList.vue` has none | **Real gap vs our own doc** (P3) |
| Purple checkmarks (read receipts) | Unread dot in gutter + read/unread actions (`InboxList.vue:566-573`) | **Justified divergence** — spec separates receipt vs local read |
| Right contact card; clicking name searches sender | `ContactPane.vue` name button → `senderSearch` → `from:"addr"` (`App.vue:702-703`); "Recent cached mail" (4 cached rows) | **Matches reference** (BROWSE-15) |
| Purple selection bar / focused row | Focus Stone fill + 4px Dusk Lavender bar (DESIGN gap 4) | **Matches reference** |
| Right-aligned dates | `.row-time` compact dates (`InboxList.vue:596`) | **Matches reference** |
| Results keyboard nav preserving query; Back restores results | J/K in list; `restoreSearch` (`useMailbox.ts:492-508`) restores query/rows/cursor/focus | **Matches spec contract BROWSE-09** |
| Loading / empty / error states | `list-state` "Loading Search…", distinct empty strings per case (`:1925`), `.recovery-banner` + Retry (`:1916-1919`), coverage `role=status` (`:1909`) | **Matches/exceeds reference** on honesty; Retry dead for syntax errors (see §8) |
| Coverage disclosure (offline/incomplete) | Explicit: "Cached content only — incomplete mailbox coverage…", "15 search results loaded · total unknown", per-page "No matches on this candidate page…" | **Exceeds reference** — Principle 1 strength |
| Paged results | `.list-more` "Continue searching older mail" (`:1945`) | **Justified divergence** — disclosed, honest |

# 3. HEURISTICS (Nielsen, scored 0–4, OUR search experience)

| # | Heuristic | Score | Justification |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Visibility of system status | **4** | Loading ("Searching… coverage not yet known."), error, empty, coverage all explicit, in words, `role=status`/`alert`; stale-response tokens prevent wrong-state display |
| 2 | Match between system and real world | **3** | Gmail-like operators feel natural, but "AND binds before OR" and the unsupported-list are spec-speak, not plain language; no glosses |
| 3 | User control and freedom | **3** | Back/Esc/undo exist and restore state; but Esc in the input exits the whole search context in one keystroke, no visible clear-X, and Retry is a dead control on syntax errors |
| 4 | Consistency and standards | **3** | Tight adherence to our own design system; but search uses a labeled form + ghost buttons while the command palette uses a bordered 16px input + highlighted rows — same job, two vocabularies |
| 5 | Error prevention | **2** | Grammar is validated only at submit; `subject:` or parens fail after Enter; no inline feedback while typing |
| 6 | Recognition rather than recall | **2** | Operator grammar must be recalled from a prose paragraph; zero suggestions, zero recent queries, no placeholder example in the empty input |
| 7 | Flexibility and efficiency of use | **3** | `/` shortcut, header glyph, palette command, sender-search from contact name, cached-only toggle, full session restore on Back; no recent queries/autocomplete |
| 8 | Aesthetic and minimalist design | **2** | The search block is the heaviest chrome in the shell: label + input + 2 buttons + checkbox + 2 paragraphs ≈ 6 lines above the list; "Search" and "Back to previous context" buttons carry real visual weight |
| 9 | Recognize/diagnose/recover from errors | **3** | Error names the exact unsupported syntax and offers edit/Retry/cached-only; but "…-exclusions.." double period and Retry re-fails identically on a deterministic parse error |
| 10 | Help and documentation | **2** | Help is always visible (good) but one dense 75ch paragraph, no examples, no operator+gloss structure |

**Total: 27/40** — solidly in the normal 20–32 band; strengths are status honesty and recovery, weaknesses are recognition (6), prevention (5), and chrome weight (8).

# 4. COGNITIVE LOAD (8-item checklist)

Flow: open (`/`/glyph) → type → Enter → loading → results / empty / error → "Continue searching older mail".
1. **Single focus** — PASS. Input owns focus on open; after submit, focus moves to the first result row.
2. **Chunking** — FAIL. Guidance is one unchunked prose paragraph plus a separate "not supported" sentence; the form block mixes input, two actions, a toggle, and two text blocks at equal weight.
3. **Grouping** — PASS (with note). Results are grouped by date captions; sender grouping absent but the 132px sender column gives a stable scan column.
4. **Visual hierarchy** — FAIL. "Find mail" label, input, both buttons, checkbox and both paragraphs are visually near-equal (all 12px, mostly `text-secondary`); the active query is never echoed as a header over results.
5. **One thing at a time** — PASS. Open → type → submit → results is strictly sequential; states replace each other.
6. **Minimal choices** — PASS. Max visible decision options: error state shows Retry + edit + cached-only + Back = 4 controls; **no decision point exceeds 4 options**.
7. **Working memory** — FAIL. User must hold the operator grammar, quoting rules, AND-before-OR precedence, the 512-**byte** cap, and the fact that Esc exits the whole context.
8. **Progressive disclosure** — PARTIAL (not counted as failure). Coverage/error lines appear only in context (good); but help is static full text and there is no staged disclosure of advanced options.

**Failures: 3 of 8** (chunking, visual hierarchy, working memory), 1 partial. Decision points >4 options: none.

# 5. EMOTIONAL JOURNEY (peak-end)

- **Found:** peak = first paint of dense results with the violet focus bar on row 1 plus the honest line "15 search results loaded · total unknown" — confidence comes from exactness (counts, dates, coverage). End = open a result → Back restores query, rows, cursor and focus (`restoreSearch`, BROWSE-09) — a genuinely trust-building round trip.
- **No results:** peak = the empty line, which honestly distinguishes "No matches on this candidate page. Continue scanning older mail below." from "No matching conversations in the searched content." plus the cached-coverage caveat — trust is preserved precisely because the UI refuses to claim "nothing exists" (BROWSE-19). Erosion risk: if the user misses the coverage line, "No matching conversations" can still read as absolute.
- **Syntax error:** peak = alarm at the coral-ish recovery banner "Could not load Search: unsupported search syntax. …-exclusions.." — informative, but (a) the double period reads as sloppiness at exactly the trust moment, (b) the form stays up top while the error renders in the list area (split attention), and (c) **Retry re-submits the identical query and fails identically** — a dead control, the exact anti-pattern in PRODUCT.md. Trust erodes here more than anywhere in the flow.

# 6. AI SLOP VERDICT

A Linear/Notion/Raycast-fluent user would **largely trust** this: warm-dark flat plane, 36px rows, one violet signal, exact counts, honest "total unknown". They would **pause** at: (1) the search form is the one surface that doesn't speak command-palette — a labeled form with two chunky ghost buttons instead of the bordered input + highlighted rows vocabulary used 1cm away in the Commands overlay (**component-vocabulary inconsistency across surfaces**); (2) "…-exclusions.." double period (microcopy slop); (3) the prose help paragraph where every comparable tool shows operator+gloss rows; (4) DESIGN.md promises a row attachment glyph that the code doesn't render (**state/completeness mismatch between register and surface**); (5) unstyled native `type=search` clear-X; (6) no placeholder in the empty input. Verdict: **not slop-tier, but "subtly off" in the form block and microcopy — exactly the class of detail this user notices.**

# 7. STRENGTHS

1. **Honest coverage reporting** — `search-coverage` four-way copy ("Searching… coverage not yet known." / cached-incomplete / online page-scan disclosure), "total unknown", per-page empty vs global empty, and `cached_incomplete` pinning `searchCachedOnly` (`useMailbox.ts:423`) so reconnection can't reinterpret cached cursors. This is Principle 1 implemented literally, and it exceeds the Superhuman reference, which discloses nothing.
2. **Session restoration** — `captureContext`/`restoreSearch` (`App.vue:820,847-850`; `useMailbox.ts:492`) preserve query, rows, cursor, coverage and focus across open→Back; stale async fences (`navigationToken`, `listToken`, `invalidateSearchIntent`) mean a slow search can never overwrite a newer context (spec's async-safety contract).
3. **Sender search from the contact pane with honest limits** — clicking the name runs `from:"addr"`, and "Recent cached mail" is exactly 4 cached rows, never invented on failure (`App.vue:712` catch → empty), matching BROWSE-15 without importing Superhuman's enrichment scope.

# 8. PRIORITY ISSUES

1. **P1 — Error state contains a dead control and a typo.** `subject:` → `.recovery-banner` "Could not load Search: unsupported search syntax. …-exclusions**..**" (`App.vue:1916-1919` adds a period to `errorText` which already ends with one, `:1690`) + a **Retry button that re-runs the identical failing query** (deterministic parse error). Violates the "dead controls that look actionable" anti-reference and weakens the error-recovery heuristic. Fix: parse on input and show the specific syntax error inline before submit; suppress Retry when `listError.field === 'searchQuery'`; fix the double period. Addressed by **`/impeccable critique`** (error-state honesty pass on App.vue/useMailbox.ts).
2. **P2 — Operator help is one dense prose paragraph, not the reference's scannable operator+gloss list.** `#search-help` (`App.vue:1908`) forces recall of 6 rules. Fix: render supported operators as two-column rows (`from:` / "from sender", `to:`, `subject:`, `"…"` / exact phrase, `AND` `OR` / combine, `-term` / exclude) plus one explicit "Not supported: dates, labels, cc/bcc, parentheses" line — same visual language as Superhuman's Tips but only our real grammar. Addressed by **`/impeccable design`**.

- The QA captures show a duplicated "Search" in the top strip (fixture workspace-strip button + the active context tab "Search" per DESIGN gap 1) — preview-harness artifact, but confusing in screenshots.

Search overlay: full-height dark panel, "Search" label + X close; left column = contact suggestions (name + email, two-column rows) above a hairline, then recent query terms as plain rows with a full-width gray keyboard-selection bar; right column = "Tips": ~17 operators each as operator (mono, light) over a plain-English gloss (gray, smaller) — from:, to:, quoted phrases, has:attachment, subject:, in:sent/in:inbox/-in:inbox/in:label, is:unread/starred/shared, before:/after: dates, older_than:/newer_than:. 2. Search results: the query becomes the list header with an X to clear; results grouped by sender with "(count)"; rows carry label chips, bold subject + gray snippet, purple read checkmarks, paperclip, right-aligned date; selected row = dark fill + purple left bar (same "you are here" language as our focused row); PDF attachment chips under rows; right-hand contact card for the searched correspondent. Scope we intentionally do NOT copy (PRODUCT.md anti-reference, spec U-items): the extended operator grammar, read-receipt checkmarks, contact enrichment, ranking claims. Visual/interaction reference we SHOULD match: operator+gloss tips in our own grammar, query visibility, suggestions/recent queries, sender grouping, keyboard-highlight rows. ## Design Health Score — 27/40 (Acceptable, top of band) | # | Heuristic | Score | Key issue | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | Visibility of system status | 4 | Loading/error/empty/coverage all explicit in words (role=status/alert); stale-response fences | | 2 | Match system / real world | 3 | "AND binds before OR" + unsupported-list is spec-speak; no glosses | | 3 | User control and freedom | 3 | Back/Esc/restore exist; but Esc in input exits whole context at once; no visible clear; Retry is dead on syntax errors | | 4 | Consistency and standards | 3 | Form+buttons vocabulary differs from command palette's input+rows vocabulary 1cm away | | 5 | Error prevention | 2 | Grammar validated only at submit; no inline feedback while typing; 512-char attr vs 512-byte parser mismatch | | 6 | Recognition rather than recall | 2 | Grammar must be recalled from a prose paragraph; no suggestions, no recent queries, no placeholder example | | 7 | Flexibility and efficiency | 3 | `/`, header glyph, palette, sender-search, cached-only toggle, full session restore; no autocomplete | | 8 | Aesthetic and minimalist design | 2 | Search block is the heaviest chrome in the shell: label + input + 2 buttons + checkbox + 2 paragraphs ≈ 6 lines | | 9 | Error recovery | 3 | Error names exact cause + offers edit/Retry/cached-only; but "..-exclusions.." double period and Retry re-fails identically | | 10 | Help and documentation | 2 | Always visible (good) but one dense 75ch paragraph, no operator+gloss structure, no examples | ## Anti-patterns verdict LLM: not slop-tier — a Linear/Notion/Raycast-fluent user largely trusts it (warm-dark flat plane, 36px rows, one violet signal, exact counts, honest "total unknown") — but pauses at: form block not speaking palette vocabulary; double-period microcopy; prose help where comparable tools show operator+gloss rows; DESIGN.md promises a row attachment glyph the code doesn't render; unstyled native type=search clear-X; no input placeholder. Detector (detect.mjs --json src, exit 2): 6 findings, all advisory, all in src/assets/style.css — design-system-radius ×3 (style.css:334, 822, 962), design-system-color ×3 (663, 858, 1199, all the documented rgba(0,0,0,0.35) shadow alpha = false positives). Zero findings in any .vue/.ts. Live detect.js injection on inbox + search states: flat-type-hierarchy (11/12/16px = documented scale, FP), line-length on single-line

s (heuristic noise); no user-visible overlay shipped. The gap to the reference is recognition and chrome economy: the query-entry UI is a heavy labeled form with a prose help paragraph, while Superhuman shows a scannable operator+gloss tips column, suggestions, and a query-as-header. The single biggest opportunity: make the search block speak the same vocabulary as the command palette and the reference's tips — operator+gloss rows for OUR grammar — and fix the dead Retry / double-period error path. ## What's working 1. Honest coverage reporting (Principle 1 implemented literally): four-way coverage copy, "total unknown", cached_incomplete pinning, per-page empty vs global empty, stale-async fences. Sender search from contact pane with honest limits: from:"addr" plus exactly-4 "Recent cached mail" rows, never invented on failure (BROWSE-15). ## Priority issues - **P1 — Dead Retry + double-period in the error state.** `subject:` → recovery banner "Could not load Search: unsupported search syntax. …-exclusions.." (errorText App.vue:1690 already ends with "."; template adds another) and Retry re-runs the identical failing query. Violates the "dead controls that look actionable" anti-reference. Fix: local per-account recent queries + cached-contact matches as arrow-navigable rows under #mail-query. → /impeccable polish (interaction pass on .mail-search). - **P2 — Query/context chrome: heavy form block, duplicated Back, aggressive Esc.** 6 lines of chrome; Search submit + "Back to previous context" buttons compete and duplicate the header Back glyph; Esc in the input both hides the form and exits the search context in one keystroke; no visible clear-X. # Superhuman search, broken down — and our implementation reviewed against it

## 1. What the two Superhuman screenshots show

**Search overlay (empty query).** A full-height dark panel: "Search" label + **X** close. Left column: *contact suggestions* (name + email in two columns), a hairline, then *recent query terms* as plain rows with a full-width gray keyboard-selection bar on the arrow-highlighted one. Right column: **"Tips"** — ~17 operators, each as *operator in mono on one line + plain-English gloss in dim text on the next* (`from:nicole` / "from Nicole", `"be brilliant"` / 'contains "be brilliant"', `-in:inbox` / "not in the Inbox", `older_than:3d` / "more than 3 days ago"…). No cards, no shadows, ~13–14px type, generous pitch.

**Search results.** The query becomes the **list header** with an X to clear. Results are **grouped by sender with `(count)`**; rows carry a label chip, bold subject + gray snippet on one line, a purple checkmark, paperclip, right-aligned date. Selected row = dark fill + **purple left bar** — the same "you are here" language as our focused row. PDF attachment chips sit under affected rows, and a contact card for the searched correspondent sits on the right.

**Scope verdict:** we deliberately do *not* copy the extended grammar (`in:`, `is:`, dates, `has:attachment`), read-receipt checkmarks, or contact enrichment — that's product scope, per our anti-reference. What we *should* match: operator+gloss tips adapted to **our** grammar, query visibility, suggestions/recent queries, sender grouping, keyboard-highlight rows.

## 2. Side-by-side with our implementation

| Superhuman | Ours | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Overlay input, `/` to open, focus on open | In-flow form above the list, `/`, header glyph, focus moved to input | Justified divergence (Principle 3), keyboard parity achieved |
| Contact suggestions + recent queries, keyboard-highlighted | **None** | **Real gap** |
| Tips: operator + gloss, scannable two-column list | One dense prose paragraph (`#search-help`) | **Real gap** — recognition vs recall |
| Query-as-header + X to clear | Editable input persists; "Back to previous context" button; Esc hides form *and* exits context | Partial — editable query is per our spec, but no echo/clear, Esc overloaded |
| Sender grouping with (count) | Flat list, date captions, 132px sender column | Justified divergence; grouping helps `from:` queries (P3) |
| Label chips / PDF chips in rows | None (label: unsupported — correct); DESIGN.md *promises* an attachment glyph the code doesn't render | Gap vs our own doc (P3) |
| Purple selection bar, right-aligned dates, right contact card + name-click searches sender | Focus Stone fill + 4px lavender bar; compact dates; ContactPane name → `from:"addr"` | **Matches reference** |
| Loading / empty / error states | Distinct honest states + coverage line + Retry | **Exceeds reference** on honesty — except Retry is dead on syntax errors |
| Coverage disclosure | Explicit four-way copy, "total unknown", per-page vs global empty | **Exceeds reference** — our Principle 1 strength |

## 3. Design Health Score: **27/40** (Acceptable, top of band)

| # | Heuristic | Score | Key issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Visibility of system status | 4 | Loading/error/empty/coverage all explicit, `role=status`/`alert` |
| 2 | Match system / real world | 3 | "AND binds before OR" is spec-speak; no glosses |
| 3 | User control and freedom | 3 | Esc exits whole context at once; no visible clear; dead Retry |
| 4 | Consistency and standards | 3 | Form+buttons vs palette input+rows vocabulary, 1cm apart |
| 5 | Error prevention | 2 | Grammar validated only at submit; char-vs-byte 512 mismatch |
| 6 | Recognition rather than recall | 2 | No suggestions, no recent queries, no placeholder, prose help |
| 7 | Flexibility and efficiency | 3 | `/`, glyph, palette, sender-search, cached-only, full restore |
| 8 | Aesthetic and minimalist | 2 | Search block ≈ 6 lines of chrome, heaviest in the shell |
| 9 | Error recovery | 3 | Names cause + suggests fixes, but `..` double period and Retry re-fails identically |
| 10 | Help and documentation | 2 | Always visible, but one dense 75ch paragraph |

Cognitive load: **3 of 8 checklist failures** (chunking, visual hierarchy, working memory); no decision point exceeds 4 options. Detector: 6 advisory findings, all in `style.css` (radius scale ×3, documented shadow alpha ×3 = FPs); zero in `.vue`/`.ts`; live browser run: no console errors, no layout/contrast issues.

## 4. Priority issues

- **P1 — Dead Retry + double period in the error state.** `subject:` → "Could not load Search: unsupported search syntax. …-exclusions**..**" and Retry re-submits the identical query, failing identically — the exact "dead controls that look actionable" anti-pattern. *Fix:* validate on input with the specific inline error, suppress Retry when `listError.field === 'searchQuery'`, fix the period.
- **P2 — Operator help is prose, not the reference's operator+gloss list.** *Fix:* two-column rows for our real grammar (`from:`/"from sender", `"…"`/exact phrase, `AND`/`OR`, `-term`/exclude) + one "Not supported: dates, labels, Cc/Bcc, parentheses" line.
- **P2 — No suggestions or recent queries under the input.** *Fix:* local recent queries + cached-contact matches as arrow-navigable rows under the input.

1. **Honest coverage reporting** — "Cached content only — incomplete mailbox coverage…", "15 search results loaded · total unknown", per-page vs global empty, `cached_incomplete` pinning, stale-response fences. Beats the reference, which discloses nothing.
2. **Session restoration** — query/rows/cursor/coverage/focus survive open→Back (BROWSE-09); a slow search can never overwrite a newer context.
3. **Sender search from the contact pane with honest limits** — `from:"addr"` + exactly 4 "Recent cached mail" rows, never invented.

---
name: implement
description: Implement an Email OS feature, bug fix, or approved plan from a task description or repository document. Use when asked to implement a scoped change in this repo. Delegates implementation to the local persona-feature-engineer agent.
---

# Implement

Implement the requested change in Email OS. The request can be a task description, an approved plan, or a path to a repository document with a specific item to implement. No ticket service is required.

Usage: `/skill:implement <task description or document path and item>`

All repository paths below are relative to the repository root. The local persona definition is `.pi/agents/persona-feature-engineer.md` from the repository root. Runtimes that mirror these documents through symlinks keep this path authoritative; follow the target, not the mirror location.

## 1. Establish the task

- Read the request and referenced documents. Identify the goal, acceptance criteria, non-goals, and affected code.
- If the request names a broad document, ask which item to implement. Do not treat every proposed feature in that document as approved work.
- Ask for clarification if a product, architecture, data migration, or scope decision is missing. Do not invent requirements.
- Inspect the working-tree status. Preserve pre-existing edits and keep one writer per checkout.

## 2. Gather repository context

Use local code and documentation, not external wiki or code-graph services:

- `README.md` for the project entry points and document map.
- `docs/development.md` for setup, commands, profile isolation, and validation gates.
- `docs/adr/0001-single-account-desktop-email-client.md` for accepted first-build scope.
- The relevant slice or UX contract under `docs/`, and the relevant section of `docs/superhuman-browsing-implementation-plan.md` or `superhuman-email-browsing-ux-spec.md` for browsing work.
- `ARCHITECTURE.md` only as a proposal, not as an inventory of implemented behavior. The PRD and older research do not authorize scope expansion.
- Current code and tests to confirm actual behavior. Escalate material conflicts between the task, accepted contracts, and implementation.

Find the affected seam:

- `crates/mail-core/`: Rust mail core, DTOs, SQLite, Gmail auth/provider/cache/sync/actions.
- `src/` and `tests/`: Vue 3/TypeScript UI, IPC adapter, and frontend tests.
- `src-tauri/`: thin Tauri 2 native shell and command/event bridge.
- `src/lib/ipc/generated.ts`: generated wire contract. Never edit it by hand; change the Rust DTOs and run `mise run gen:ts`.

Follow existing conventions and any applicable project instructions. Do not invent a separate coding-standard source.

## 3. Delegate implementation

Using this skill authorizes one implementation subagent. Do not ask the user to request delegation again.

- Read your runtime's subagent guidance and the local persona definition before launch.
- Start `persona-feature-engineer` through the runtime's native subagent mechanism: the `subagent` tool in pi, the Task tool with subagent type `persona-feature-engineer` in Claude Code, or the custom agent `persona-feature-engineer` in Codex. Inherit the parent model unless the user specifies another one.
- Give the child a self-contained brief: explicit repository cwd, goal, acceptance criteria, non-goals, relevant files and contracts, pre-existing edits, edit boundary, required checks, verification method, and expected evidence.
- Tell the child to execute directly. It must not use this skill to delegate again or start other agents.
- Leave implementation to the child. Do not edit the same checkout while it works. Follow native async completion notifications; do not poll or sleep.
- Route blocking decisions to the user when the task and project instructions do not already answer them. Do not approve new scope on the user's behalf.

If subagent tooling is unavailable before launch, read the persona definition and do the work directly under its rules. State that fallback. If a launch or runtime fails, stop and report the failure and partial work state. Do not silently switch execution methods.

If you are already the delegated implementation child, follow the persona and execute the task directly. Do not launch another agent.

## 4. Test and verify

Use `mise.toml` and `docs/development.md` as the command source. Select the checks that cover the changed seam:

| Change | Checks |
| --- | --- |
| Rust mail core | `mise run test:core`, `mise run lint:core` |
| Rust DTOs or IPC | Regenerate with `mise run gen:ts`; run `mise run check:contract`, core tests, and affected UI/native checks |
| Vue/TypeScript UI | `mise run test:ui`, `mise run typecheck`, `mise run build:web` |
| Tauri shell or bridge | `mise run check:native`, `mise run test:native`, plus affected core/UI checks |
| Cross-cutting work | `mise run check` plus web build and native checks where affected |

Add focused regression tests. Capture before-and-after behavior as required by the persona. Run the relevant checks against the final code and report exact commands and outcomes.

- Use `mise run dev:web` for the synthetic, in-memory browser preview. Use `mise run dev:native` for native fixture verification. Use a background terminal for long-running dev processes.
- Browser success is not proof of SQLite durability, native IPC, macOS WKWebView behavior, Keychain, OAuth, or Gmail convergence. Run the relevant native path or report the native gate as blocked and ask how to verify it.
- Default to synthetic fixtures and fake-provider tests. Do not enable Gmail mode, request OAuth grants, connect a real mailbox, or perform real provider writes without explicit operator approval for the disposable-account path.
- Never expose credentials or real mailbox content in logs, screenshots, or reports. Preserve profile isolation and existing permission boundaries.
- Do not install OS packages or change system configuration merely to unblock a native check. Report missing prerequisites.

## Rust dependency documentation

Check `Cargo.lock` for the exact resolved crate version before looking up its API. If multiple versions exist, identify the one used by the affected package. Do not use `latest` or change a dependency merely to match newer documentation.

- Item index: `https://docs.rs/{crate}/{version}/{crate_underscored}/all.html`
- Specific item: `https://docs.rs/{crate}/{version}/{crate_underscored}/struct.Foo.html` (or `trait.`, `enum.`, `fn.`)
- Source browser: `https://docs.rs/crate/{crate}/{version}/source/`

Use the same version-specific approach for frontend and Tauri documentation, based on `package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, and `Cargo.lock`.

## 5. Return the result

Review the child's final diff and evidence against the task. Do not equate a successful agent exit with a verified feature. Report:

- What changed and which acceptance criteria it meets.
- Changed file paths.
- Exact checks and results, including failures or skipped gates.
- Before-and-after verification evidence and artifact paths.
- Remaining risks, blockers, and decisions needed.

Do not claim completion when required verification is missing. Do not commit, push, publish, or update a pull request unless the user authorizes it. Return pull-request-ready evidence when publication is not authorized.

description: Implement scoped features with focused tests and before-and-after verification evidence
advertise: true

# Feature Engineer Persona

Work as a production engineer. Implement the assigned feature in the existing system. Meet the requirements and the applicable coding standards.

Write in the style of ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English. Use short sentences, direct instructions, and consistent terms. Preserve exact code identifiers, commands, and technical terms.

## Scope and authority

- Read the task, acceptance criteria, project instructions, and relevant code before you edit.
- Follow the coding standards for the project and language.
- If the code does not meet the requirements, change the code.
- Preserve existing user-visible and external behavior outside the task scope. Change existing behavior when the requirements call for it.
- Refactor production code when this makes the feature clear and maintainable. Do not preserve obsolete code only because it exists. Keep refactoring within the task scope.
- Do not add unrequested features, dependencies, abstractions, or cleanup.
- Make routine implementation choices within the approved requirements and project patterns. Do not invent product requirements or make unapproved architecture, public API, migration, or scope decisions.
- If requirements conflict or a decision is missing, stop the affected work and ask the supervisor. Do not guess.
- Do the assigned work yourself. Do not start other subagents unless the parent explicitly authorizes delegation.

## Gather information

Use the sources that apply to the task:

- The task brief and project instructions.
- Relevant code, tests, local documentation, and coding-standard rules.
- The Tolaria wiki for documented behavior, when it is available and relevant.
- The Frontier Platform CodeGraph for code relationships, when it is available and relevant.

Check documentation against the current code. Do not assume that an unavailable source was checked. If a missing source blocks a correct implementation, ask for access or the required information. Otherwise, state the limitation and continue with the available evidence.

## Implement and test

1. Define the expected result from the acceptance criteria.
2. Capture the before state before you edit production code.
3. Make a focused, coherent change. Follow the existing project patterns.
4. Add or update short, focused automated tests. Cover the requested behavior, relevant failure cases, and behavior that must stay unchanged.
5. Run the relevant tests, type checks, lint checks, and build checks available in the project. Do not weaken tests or checks to make the change pass.
6. Verify the feature through its user-facing or external interface.
7. Review the final diff for scope, correctness, and unrelated changes.

Use automated tests to prove behavior. Manual checks do not replace tests. Passing tests alone do not replace verification through the actual interface.

## Verify the change

Work without verification is not done. Capture a comparable before state and after state. If the feature does not exist before the change, record its absence or the current failure.

- **UI change:** Run the app or Storybook. Use the affected flow. Capture screenshots before and after the change.
- **Backend or CLI change:** Call the endpoint or run the command. Record the inputs, relevant environment, exit status or HTTP status, and returned output before and after the change.
- **Prompt or eval change:** Run the relevant evals before and after the change. Record the configuration and both results.
- **Other change:** Use the actual consumer or execution path. Record reproducible before-and-after evidence.

Use safe local or test data. Do not mutate production systems, send messages, or perform destructive operations without explicit approval. Remove secrets and personal data from evidence.

Capture the after state when the tests pass. If you change the code after verification, rerun the affected checks and capture new after evidence. Replace evidence that no longer represents the final code.

If you cannot capture the baseline or run the change, stop and ask how to verify it. Do not claim the work is done or fabricate evidence.

## Escalation

Follow the runtime's supervisor-routing instructions. When available, use `contact_supervisor` with `reason: "need_decision"` for a blocking question. State the blocker, the decision needed, and the relevant options. Wait for the answer before you continue the affected work.

If the supervisor tool is unavailable, return a blocked result with the question and current work state. Do not report success.

## Guardrails

- Do not inspect Git history. Do not use history, blame, or old revisions to investigate past changes. You may use Git status and working-tree diffs to inspect current work.
- Preserve unrelated and pre-existing edits. Do not reset, discard, or overwrite another contributor's work.
- Do not commit, push, open or update a merge request, or publish changes unless the task authorizes it.
- Follow inherited tool, safety, and project instructions. This persona does not expand your permissions.

## Result and evidence

Return a concise handoff:

- **Status:** complete or blocked.
- **Implemented:** what changed and which requirements it meets.
- **Files:** changed file paths.
- **Checks:** exact commands, results, and any failures or skipped checks.
- **Verification:** before-and-after observations, relevant outputs, and screenshot or artifact paths.
- **Risks or blockers:** remaining limitations and required decisions.

Put verification evidence in the merge request description, not in a comment, when the task authorizes a merge request update. Otherwise, return merge-request-ready evidence to the parent. Do not create or update a merge request only to store evidence.

# Development guide

This repository contains two deliberately separate native profiles: the durable
synthetic fixture slice (Slice 01) and an explicit Gmail profile built in stages.
Slice 02 adds system-browser OAuth/PKCE, a macOS Keychain credential store,
bounded inbox caching, and background sync. Slice 03 adds opt-in, durable Gmail
archive/unarchive and explicit read/unread actions; Gmail remains read-only until
the user explicitly requests the broader Google `gmail.modify` permission.
Slice 04 adds a local-only plain-text composer and durable draft recovery, but
still does not send/delete mail or expose arbitrary labels. Opening a message
never marks it read. UX-05 adds bounded multi-select and durable bulk
archive/read group processing with one-level partial group Undo; the browser
preview remains synthetic and in-memory. See
the slice contracts for individual acceptance scope. UX-08 adds narrow Gmail-mode
Star/Unstar singles/groups, durable Undo/reconciliation, cache-only Starred and a
single cached starred filter; see [its contract and validation ledger](ux-08-stars.md).
The legacy native fixture remains archive-only; unsupported star controls are
absent there. No real provider writes are authorized by implementation tests.
UX-06 adds one durable local
sender/domain split over Inbox, exact cached-count badges, and a single unread
filter. See [the saved-split contract](ux-06-saved-split.md) for matching,
keyboard navigation, cache coverage, and persistence boundaries.

## Layout

| Path | Owner |
|---|---|
| `crates/mail-core/` | Rust DTOs, fixture core, Gmail provider/auth/cache/sync/actions, SQLite, profile locks |
| `src/`, `tests/`, `package.json`, configs | Vue 3/TypeScript frontend, IPC adapter and tests |
| `src/lib/ipc/generated.ts` | **Generated** — do not edit by hand; regenerate with `mise run gen:ts` |
| `src-tauri/` | Thin Tauri 2 shell: typed mail/draft/close commands, `mailbox_changed` and `drafts_changed` hints, fixture/Gmail profile selection and lifecycle |
| `mise.toml` | Project tasks (see below) |

## UX-09 increment A: read-only provider mail

The **Provider mail** rail entry (Gmail native or labelled browser preview) opens
a bounded destination browser for Sent, provider Drafts, All Mail, Spam, Trash
and user labels. Search covers the loaded catalog; Show more expands it. It is
not mailbox search. All Mail excludes Spam/Trash. Every page contains at most
25 conversations, at most 16 MiB of serialized thread DTOs, and no exact total.
The read-only drawer intentionally has no triage/reply controls. Its page remains
mounted during a reader visit; closing the drawer returns to the prior inbox
context. This is not yet the roadmap's integrated main-list destination context.

Native commands `list_provider_destinations(accountId, cached)` and
`browse_provider_destination(request)` run off the UI thread, require the active
account, and use readonly Gmail APIs. Page cursors carry account+destination
identity and a bounded opaque provider token; they grant no authority.
A separate SQLite table retains one catalog and up to 20 destination snapshots
(latest successful page per retained destination), independent of inbox discovery,
history and operation recovery. **Use saved catalog/page** is explicit and
timestamped; provider failures are never silently converted to saved success or
an empty list. Restart retains these snapshots; disconnect clears them.

Provider Drafts are read-only snapshots, **not** the app's local editable drafts.
The native fixture rejects both provider commands; browser preview models them
in memory only. Label/Move, label badges on ordinary inbox rows, palette integration,
and saved-view/search criteria are not implemented here. After rebasing onto
`b4972ee`, the UX-06/07/08 contracts are preserved but not extended by this
increment. See [the increment contract](ux-09-provider-destinations.md)
for evidence and remaining gates.

## Tooling

All commands run through [mise](https://mise.jdx.dev) (pinned: node 24.4.1,
pnpm 10.18.0, rust 1.89.0). First-time setup:

```sh
mise trust           # after inspecting the repository's mise.toml
mise install         # install the project-pinned runtimes/tools
mise run install:ui   # locked frontend dependencies (pnpm install --frozen-lockfile)
```

Rust dependencies resolve via the committed `Cargo.lock` on first `cargo`/`mise` use;
no global configuration is needed.

### Local-only `mise.local.toml`

`mise.local.toml` is **gitignored and machine-local** (`/mise.local.toml` in `.gitignore`):
it holds no secrets and must never be committed. Create it in every checkout/worktree you

1:# UX-07 — Historical search and return
3:Implemented journey: `/` (or Search) → submit → result → reader → Back to the same query, loaded results, focused reference and list anchor → Back to the previous browsing context. Search does not mark messages read. Existing explicit setters, selection, Undo, Activity and local-only drafts remain in use.
7:`search_mail(SearchRequest) → SearchPage` and `cancel_search_mail()` are narrow, read-only commands. Requests carry the active account, query, continuation and an explicit cached-only choice. Rust owns validation and evaluation; the browser fake mirrors it for synthetic preview only.
11:- Unqualified text searches subject, known From/To names and addresses, and cached plain-text message bodies. `from:`, `to:` and `subject:` restrict those fields. A conversation matches over its known message stack (criteria may match different messages).
12:- Unknown operators, parentheses/braces, escapes, unmatched quotes, missing values and dangling operators reject with `invalid_request/searchQuery`. Colons inside a quoted phrase are literal text. No Cc/Bcc, labels, date/time operators or implicit timezone conversion. Message timestamps remain UTC facts; existing localized list date grouping is unchanged.
17:The provider enumerates **20 mailbox candidates per page**, without an INBOX filter and with Spam/Trash excluded (`includeSpamTrash=false`). It reads each candidate through the existing paced/authenticated/cancellable thread reader and sync's 16 MiB aggregate retained-data budget and evaluates the same AST as cached mode. This deliberate first implementation avoids silently substituting Gmail's tokenization/stemming for our substring semantics. It reaches older archived mail beyond inbox discovery, but is a **progressive scan**, not indexed Gmail search: a selective query may need multiple empty candidate pages before finding a match. The UI explicitly says this and keeps continuation available on empty pages. Totals are unknown. Provider-side query acceleration is deferred until it can provably preserve the supported semantics.
19:Provider failures (including auth expiry, rate limits, missing/invalid responses) stay errors, not empty results. The user can retry or explicitly choose cached-only search. A known disconnected/offline account uses the local cache with an incompleteness disclosure. A failure while continuing preserves loaded rows and the exact retry cursor. Missing provider threads are omitted; opening an evicted result performs a visible exact-ID read, and a missing body/result produces the existing reader error, never a substitute conversation.
21:Cursors are bound to account and exact query. The frontend fences list/detail/account/navigation generations, deduplicates account-scoped identities, and cancels provider search on replacement/context exit/unmount. Lifecycle cancellation and SQLite generation checks also fence native writes. Search pages, explicit missing-result loads and action rehydration additionally capture the store connection's observation revision before provider reads. Admission rejects with `busy` if any intervening store write occurred, including history/deletion checkpoints or confirmed setters; an explicit retry takes a fresh observation. This deliberately conservative fence can reject an otherwise usable page after an unrelated write, rather than overwrite newer mailbox facts. Contact-history queries are explicitly cached-only, so J/K never initiates or cancels provider traversal.
25:Search-only conversations have a separate 100-conversation retention budget tracked in `gmail_search_cache`. Admission does not advance/reset inbox discovery or history checkpoints, and search-only rows do not appear as inbox discoveries. A normally observed inbox row is promoted out of search-only membership. Inbox discovery's cap excludes search-only rows. Cached search coverage remains incomplete; it cannot reliably infer Spam/Trash membership where those facts were never cached.
27:Search admission is account/generation checked and transactional. Search eviction removes bodies and unpinned facts, never durable operations, immutable operation targets, preimages or recovery snapshots. Before accepting a single or group setter, genuinely missing exact conversation references are revalidated through bounded provider reads after the normal account/capability checks. Retained message facts plus an account-scoped recovery snapshot already provide sufficient local action context; these actions do not require provider reads. Deferred action paths carry the original admission generation through provider registration, offline fallback and transactional acceptance, so reconnecting the same account cannot revive an unaccepted command from the previous lifecycle. Rehydrated rows and immutable targets/recovery snapshots are admitted in the same transaction; search eviction runs only after all group members have been considered. Durable idempotent replays do not require provider reads. A committed setter captures its existing durable recovery snapshot before any subsequent search eviction. Disconnect clears search membership with the rest of account data.
31:Activating the known contact name starts a From search; Copy name / Copy email remain independent explicit clipboard actions. Up to four actual cached matches are shown as recent-email links, from a bounded result page. These are local known history, not invented enrichment or a claim to provider-complete recency.
35:Synthetic tests cover the full archived-result/reader/Back/previous-context journey, query grammar, editable shortcut safety, explicit invalid-query errors, stale responses, duplicate pages, continuation rate limits, contact/copy separation, named transport envelopes, native older-archive admission, account/generation fencing, provider pagination/defaults, and bounded eviction preserving operation recovery. P1 regressions additionally cover search observations racing confirmed archive/read and history deletions, single/mixed-group actions after six pages evict earlier results, known expired auth versus explicit cached search, and explicit query intent surviving background refresh during deferred cancellation while still respecting newer navigation/account/disposal intents. Mounted-App regressions exercise actual reader-open, Close/Back, same-context Inbox shortcut, recent-link, J/K and utility-destination boundaries; native regressions cover disconnect/reconnect before and during rehydration, final transactional generation checks, and local recovery actions during provider network/rate-limit failures.

**Method:** `persona-feature-engineer` subagent ×2, sequential in the same checkout (one writer per checkout). Nothing committed or staged — the work is in your working tree, pull-request-ready.

### P1 — Error honesty (subagent 1)
- New `validateSearch()` in `src/lib/search.ts` mirrors the Rust grammar and returns a *specific* plain-language problem while typing (`"subject:" needs a value — e.g. subject:"example".`, unmatched quote, unsupported `(`, >512 **bytes** — the input's `maxlength` counts chars, now measured with TextEncoder like `parseSearch`).
- Invalid queries never reach `searchMail`; the results banner **hides Retry** when the error is `field: 'searchQuery'` (a deterministic parse error would re-fail identically — dead control) and points at the query instead; Retry stays for real provider errors. Double period `…-exclusions..` fixed at the source (`errorText` no longer pre-ends with a period).

### P2 — Operator+gloss help, following the reference (subagent 1)
The dense prose paragraph is now a scannable list in the Superhuman "Tips" style, restricted to our real grammar: `from:`/from sender, `to:`/to recipient, `subject:`/in subject, `"…"`/exact phrase in straight quotes, `AND` `OR`/combine terms — AND binds before OR, `-term`/exclude a term or field, plus one muted line: "Not supported: dates, labels, Cc/Bcc, parentheses."

### P3 — Suggestions under the input (subagent 1)
Session-scoped, in-memory, per-account recent queries (deduped, most-recent-first, cap 8 — deliberately **not** persisted) shown when the input is empty; typing adds cached-correspondent matches. Arrow keys move a full-width highlight, Enter fills+submits, Esc closes the list first; single-letter shortcuts stay inert inside the input (BROWSE-10 test included).

### P4 — Reference-style chrome (subagent 1)
Search context now shows a one-line **`Search: <query>` header with an X exit** (new `x` glyph in `HeaderGlyph.vue`), the form slims to one entry row + cached-only checkbox, and **Esc is two-step**: first collapses the form (context and results stay), second exits the context. UX-07 restore (query/rows/cursor/focus across reader round trips) is untouched and tested.

### P5b — Sender grouping (subagent 2)
For a single-`from:` search query, results group under captions like **`Ada Fixture (15)`** (existing `row-group` caption mechanism, non-actionable) instead of date captions; all other queries/contexts keep date captions. j/k, reader J/K, Back-anchors and auto-advance all walk the rendered order — focus never lands on a caption. ## 4. COGNITIVE LOAD — 8-item checklist on the current flow

1. **Open** (`/` or `search-trigger`): form appears, focus in input, suggestions open if recents exist — **pass**.
2. **Type with suggestions**: live filter, arrows highlight, Enter applies/submits, Esc closes — **partial fail**: listbox unbounded (up to 14 rows, no max-height/scroll), `aria-controls` dangles when the `<ul>` unmounts, Esc→ArrowDown doesn't reopen, pointer highlight doesn't scroll into view. **1 decision point with >4 options: the listbox (6 correspondents + 8 recents).**
3. **Inline error?**: specific message per keystroke, `role=alert`, doesn't block typing — **pass**.
4. **Submit**: invalid blocked client-side; valid runs; header echo appears — **pass with note**: query shown twice (header + input) after submit.
5. **Results / grouped**: sender captions for single-`from:`, date captions otherwise, coverage line above list — **pass**.
6. **Empty**: two honest variants ("No matches on this candidate page. Continue scanning older mail below." vs "No matching conversations in the searched content.") — **pass**.
7. **Error**: banner names cause; Retry hidden only for syntax — **minor fail**: "Edit the query above" points at a form that may be collapsed after Esc.
8. **More**: `data-test="done-more"` "Continue searching older mail" — **pass**.

**Failures: 2** (listbox edge cases; error copy when form collapsed). **Decision points >4 options: 1** (suggestion listbox).

## 5. EMOTIONAL JOURNEY (peak-end)

- **Found**: peak = results appearing under the "Search: \<query\>" header with honest coverage line; end = first row focused with the violet bar, ready to act. Positive, trust-building.
- **No-results**: end state is a quiet gray line — flat but honest; the per-page variant ("Continue scanning older mail below" + `done-more`) preserves agency. Neutral-honest, on-brand.
- **Syntax error**: peak-end is now corrective, not punitive — the coral inline error appears *while typing* with the exact fix ("close the quoted phrase"), submit is blocked, and the dead-Retry path is gone. Big improvement over the old "…-exclusions.." dead end.
- **Grouped from-search**: the "Ada Fixture (15)" caption delivers an immediate total + identity (peak), rows keep per-row dates; losing the date-group captions makes recency scanning rely on row dates only — acceptable, matches the reference.

## 6. AI SLOP / PRODUCT-SLOP VERDICT

A Linear/Notion/Raycast-fluent user would now **trust this surface**: the suggestions reuse the palette's exact listbox vocabulary (combobox + `aria-activedescendant` + Focus Stone/lavender highlight), the header echo + X mirrors the reference, the help reads like Raycast's operator hints, and coverage honesty exceeds the reference. Not slop. **New subtly-off details introduced by the fixes:**
1. **Query duplication**: after submit, "Search: \<query\>" header *and* the prefilled input are both visible (after/01-03) — two sources of truth for the same string, ~10 lines of chrome above the results.
2. **Suggestion listbox vs palette**: 28px rows vs palette's 36px, no height cap — close vocabulary, not identical.
3. **Help copy run-on**: "**AND OR** combine terms — AND binds before OR" (two adjacent `.search-op` spans, visible in every after screenshot).
4. **Glyph semantics**: no paperclip = "no attachment" to a scanner; unknown renders as nothing, unlike the row's 3-state read marker.
5. **Two X affordances** in one view: the native `type="search"` clear-X inside the input (after/02) and the custom `search-clear` X on the header — different glyphs, both "clear".
6. **Two-step Esc is invisible**: no hint anywhere that the first Esc only collapses the form.

## 7. STRENGTHS

1. **The error path is now honest end-to-end**: per-keystroke inline validation with exact plain-language causes → client-side gate (provider never sees invalid queries) → dead-Retry removal + single period on the banner path; 19 component tests pin all of it, including the byte-vs-char cap.
2. **One vocabulary across surfaces**: suggestions use the palette's combobox/listbox/highlight language, and BROWSE-10 inertness inside the input is regression-tested.
3. **Sender grouping shares one pure definition** (`groupRowsBySender` in both App.vue `listRows` and InboxList `items`), so j/k navigation order and visible order can never diverge, and the reader/Back/restore round-trips preserve grouping — all test-pinned.

## 8. PRIORITY ISSUES (remaining)

- **P1 — Results header has no edit affordance.** After Esc collapses the form (or after any submit→collapse), the only ways back into the query are `/` or the header glyph; the banner copy "Edit the query above" can reference a hidden form. *Why:* the reference's query-as-header is clickable/reopens the input; ours is static text. *Fix:* make `.search-results-query` a button that calls `revealSearch()` (with title/aria-label "Edit search query"), and fix the banner copy to "Edit the query — press /" when `!searchVisible`. → `/impeccable polish` on `.search-results-header` + `/impeccable clarify` on the banner copy.
- **P2 — Post-submit duplication and chrome weight.** Form stays open after submit → query shown twice, ~10 lines above the list. *Fix:* auto-collapse the form on successful submit (keep it open only while the draft differs from the submitted query or on error), making header+coverage+list the default results state exactly like the reference. → `/impeccable distill` on `.mail-search` / `.search-results-header`.
- **P2 — Suggestion listbox edge cases.** No `max-height`/`overflow` (up to 14 rows push results off-screen), `aria-controls` references an unmounted `<ul>` when closed, Esc→ArrowDown can't reopen, pointermove highlight doesn't scroll into view. *Fix:* cap height with scroll + scroll-into-view on highlight, keep the `<ul>` mounted (v-show) or bind `aria-controls` conditionally, reopen on ArrowDown when closed. → `/impeccable harden` + `/impeccable polish` on `.search-suggestions` / `onSearchInputKeydown`.
- **P3 — Attachment glyph two-visible-states.** `hasAttachments === true` → clip; `false`/`undefined` → nothing, so "unknown" is indistinguishable from "none" (inconsistent with the hollow-ring read-state convention). *Fix:* hollow/outline paperclip with "Attachment state unknown" for `undefined`, matching the read marker; or document the two-state convention in DESIGN.md §5. → `/impeccable clarify`.
- **P3 — Sender captions replace date captions entirely.** In from-searches the calendar orientation caption disappears (p5a/03 has no "January 2025" while after/03 does); also the "AND OR" help run-on. *Fix:* confirm intentional parity with the reference (results are sender-grouped there too) and note it in DESIGN.md, or nest date captions under sender captions; fix the AND/OR row copy to "AND / OR". → `/impeccable layout` / `/impeccable polish`.

## 9. MINOR OBSERVATIONS

1. "AND OR" run-on in the help row (two `.search-op` spans, one `<li>`) — reads as "ANDOR" at 12px.
2. Native `type="search"` clear-X inside the input is unstyled and duplicates the custom `search-clear` X in the same view.
3. No `placeholder` on `data-test="search-input"`; first-run (no session recents) suggestion box is empty — recognition depends wholly on the help list.
4. `maxlength="512"` counts characters while the grammar caps 512 UTF-8 bytes; now caught inline with a clear byte message (tested), so acceptable — but the attribute still permits typing that will fail.
5. `.search-coverage` sits below the 7-line help block when the form is open, so it reads as form output rather than list status; when collapsed it sits correctly under the header (after/04).
6. `search-clear` and `context-back` are duplicate exits with near-identical titles ("Clear search and return to the previous context" vs "Back to previous context").

## 10. PROVOCATIVE QUESTIONS

1. If the query header is the results' identity (as in the reference), should submitting auto-collapse the form so header+list is the default state, with the header itself clickable as the only edit path — and would that finally make search feel like one overlay vocabulary with the palette instead of a form that happens to sit in the list column?
2. Search suggestions (28px rows), palette items (36px), and the rail all use "highlighted row" language, yet each keeps its own geometry and exit affordance — how much vocabulary parity is enough before search should just be a palette mode with the query prefilled?
3. Sender grouping drops date captions in exactly the query type ("everything from X") where calendar orientation matters most — is losing that context acceptable parity, or should from-searches nest date captions under sender captions?

# Critique re-run: our search experience vs Superhuman reference (after P1-P5 fix batch)

Method: dual-agent (A: 753be25a-de1c-4d8e-aaf1-03bc83c48c34 design review · B: 744dff78-d60f-451f-8ef4-67a09d50c9be detector + browser evidence)
Baseline: 27/40 (2026-11-07T20-10-31Z snapshot). Fresh score on the fixed working tree: 34/40.

## Verification of the P1-P5 fixes
- P1 FIXED: validateSearch (search.ts:36-80) per-keystroke inline errors (role=alert, data-test=search-error); submit gated client-side — 20,026-input fuzz shows validateSearch and parseSearch agree exactly, invalid never reaches searchMail; banner hides Retry for invalid_request/searchQuery and says "Edit the query above — the same query fails again."; single period (test asserts no ".."). Live: `subject:` shows `"subject:" needs a value — e.g. subject:"example".` and no banner.
- P2 FIXED: #search-help is now 6 operator+gloss rows + 1 "Not supported: dates, labels, Cc/Bcc, parentheses." line. Nit: "AND OR" run-on row.
- P3 FIXED with edge-case half-fixes: combobox+listbox (aria-activedescendant, highlighted = Focus Stone + 4px lavender bar, palette vocabulary), up to 8 session-only recents + 6 cached-correspondent matches (from:"mailbox"), Enter applies, click applies, BROWSE-10 inert. Half-fixes: no max-height/scroll (up to 14 rows), aria-controls dangles when ul unmounts, Esc→ArrowDown doesn't reopen, pointer highlight doesn't scroll into view.
- P4 FIXED: `Search: <query>` header (16px) + X (data-test=search-clear, "Clear search and return to the previous context") + slim one-row form; Esc is three-step (close listbox → collapse form, focus to row, context stays → exit context), all tested and captured live (07/08/08b).
- P5b FIXED: single-from: searches group under `Name (count)` captions (role=presentation, non-tabbable); date captions replaced in grouped view; one pure groupRowsBySender shared by App.vue listRows and InboxList items so nav order == render order. Live: `Ada Fixture (15)` + `<script>…</script> (3)` (literal, XSS-safe).
- P5a FIXED: RowGlyph attachment paperclip, .row-attachment role=img aria-label "Has attachments", only when hasAttachments===true, before the date (16px glyph at x=1048 vs date x=1076). 18/18 fixture rows show it. Semantics gap: false and undefined both render nothing (unknown indistinguishable from none — inconsistent with 3-state read marker).

## Design Health Score — 34/40 (Good, 28-35 band; was 27)

| # | Heuristic | Was | Now | Key note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Visibility of system status | 4 | 4 | coverage role=status survives form collapse; stale fences |
| 2 | Match system / real world | 3 | 3 | plain-language errors now; "AND binds before OR" + byte-cap still spec-speak; unstyled native clear-X |
| 3 | User control and freedom | 3 | 3 | Esc steps undiscoverable; duplicate exits (header Back + search-clear X + native X); no edit path from results header |
| 4 | Consistency and standards | 3 | 3 | suggestions speak palette vocabulary but 28px rows vs palette 36px |
| 5 | Error prevention | 2 | 4 | per-keystroke validation, client gate, byte cap explained |
| 6 | Recognition rather than recall | 2 | 3 | help list + live suggestions; no placeholder; recents session-only |
| 7 | Flexibility and efficiency | 3 | 3 | `/`, glyph, palette, contact from:, restore; no operator completion |
| 8 | Aesthetic and minimalist | 2 | 3 | collapsed state slim; post-submit form stays open → ~10 lines chrome, query duplicated |
| 9 | Error recovery | 3 | 4 | inline cause while typing; dead Retry gone; banner copy can point at a collapsed form |
| 10 | Help and documentation | 2 | 4 | operator+gloss rows + unsupported line; aria-describedby wiring |

Cognitive load: 2 failures (listbox edge cases; error copy when form collapsed); 1 decision point >4 options (listbox). Detector: 6 advisory findings, all in style.css, all FP/out-of-scope for the search regions (search CSS clean, zero findings in App.vue/InboxList.vue/search.ts). Browser: zero console errors; all text passes AA 4.5 (header 14.7, secondary 7.8, unsupported 5.4, glyph 4.3 non-text pass); no overflow at 1440×900; screenshots /private/tmp/email-os-search-critique2/ 01-11.

## Remaining priority issues
- P1 — Results header is static text, no edit affordance: after Esc collapses the form, only `/` or the glyph reopens it, and the banner copy "Edit the query above" can reference a hidden form. Fix: make .search-results-query a button calling revealSearch(); adjust banner copy when !searchVisible. → /impeccable polish + clarify
- P2 — Post-submit duplication/chrome weight: form stays open after submit, query shown twice (header + input), ~10 lines above results. Fix: auto-collapse form on successful submit (keep open while draft differs or on error) so header+coverage+list is the default, like the reference. → /impeccable distill
- P2 — Suggestion listbox edge cases: no max-height/scroll, dangling aria-controls when unmounted, Esc→ArrowDown can't reopen, pointer highlight no scroll-into-view. → /impeccable harden + polish
- P3 — Attachment glyph two visible states: unknown (undefined) vs none (false) both render nothing, inconsistent with the 3-state read marker. Fix: outline paperclip "Attachment state unknown" for undefined, or document the two-state convention in DESIGN.md §5. → /impeccable clarify
- P3 — Sender captions replace date captions in from-searches (calendar orientation lost exactly where recency matters); "AND OR" help run-on. Fix: document parity or nest date captions under sender captions; copy "AND / OR". → /impeccable layout / polish

## Minor observations
- "AND OR" run-on in help row; unstyled native type=search clear-X duplicates search-clear X; no input placeholder (fresh session shows empty listbox); maxlength=512 chars vs 512-byte grammar cap (now caught inline, acceptable); coverage line sits below the 7-line help when form open (reads as form output); search-clear and context-back are near-duplicate exits.

## Questions
1. Should submitting auto-collapse the form so header+list is the default results state, with the header itself clickable as the only edit path?
2. Sender grouping drops date captions in from-searches — acceptable reference parity, or nest date captions under sender captions?
3. Remaining scope: just the P1 edit-affordance + auto-collapse (top 2), or all five remaining issues?

# Re-run critique: search vs the Superhuman reference — **34/40, up from 27/40**

**Method: dual-agent** (A: `753be25a…` design review · B: `744dff78…` detector + live browser evidence, 11 states captured at 1440×900, zero console errors)

## Design Health Score: 34/40 — "Good" band (28–35); was 27/40 "Acceptable"

| # | Heuristic | Was → Now | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Visibility of system status | 4 → 4 | coverage line survives form collapse; stale-response fences |
| 2 | Match system / real world | 3 → 3 | errors now plain-language; "AND binds before OR" still jargon |
| 3 | User control and freedom | 3 → 3 | Esc steps work but are undiscoverable; three "clear/exit" affordances coexist |
| 4 | Consistency and standards | 3 → 3 | suggestions reuse palette listbox vocabulary, but 28px vs 36px rows |
| 5 | Error prevention | **2 → 4** | per-keystroke validation, client-side submit gate, byte cap explained |
| 6 | Recognition rather than recall | **2 → 3** | operator+gloss help + live suggestions; no placeholder yet |
| 7 | Flexibility and efficiency | 3 → 3 | `/`, glyph, palette, contact-`from:`, restore; no operator completion |
| 8 | Aesthetic and minimalist | **2 → 3** | collapsed state is slim; post-submit form still open (~10 lines) |
| 9 | Error recovery | **3 → 4** | inline cause while typing; dead Retry gone; single period |
| 10 | Help and documentation | **2 → 4** | operator+gloss rows replace the prose wall |

**All five fixes verified in code, tests, and live browser:** P1 inline errors (`"subject:" needs a value — e.g. subject:"example".`, role=alert, invalid never reaches `searchMail` — 20k-input fuzz shows `validateSearch`≡`parseSearch`; Retry hidden on syntax errors, single period); P2 six operator+gloss rows + one "Not supported" line; P3 combobox/listbox suggestions (8 session recents + 6 correspondent matches, arrows/Enter/click, shortcuts inert); P4 `Search: <query>` header + X + three-step Esc (captured: Esc closes listbox → collapses form, header stays → exits context); P5b sender captions `Ada Fixture (15)` for `from:` searches (date captions replaced); P5a paperclip before the date, `role=img "Has attachments"`, 16px Graphite, only when known-true.

**Detector:** 6 advisory findings, all pre-existing style.css shadow/radius FPs — the search regions (`App.vue` search block, `InboxList.vue`, `search.ts`, `.search-*` CSS) are clean. Contrast: all text ≥5.4:1 on the app bg (AA pass).

## Remaining issues (in priority order)
- **P1 — Results header has no edit affordance.** After Esc collapses the form, only `/` reopens it, and the error banner's "Edit the query above" can point at a hidden form. Fix: make the `Search: <query>` header a button that reopens the input; adjust banner copy when the form is collapsed.
- **P2 — Post-submit duplication.** The form stays open after submit, so the query appears twice (header + prefilled input) with ~10 lines of chrome above results. Fix: auto-collapse on successful submit → header + coverage + list as the default, exactly like the reference.
- **P2 — Suggestion listbox edge cases.** No max-height/scroll (up to 14 rows push results down), `aria-controls` dangles when the list unmounts, Esc→ArrowDown can't reopen it, pointer highlight doesn't scroll into view.
- **P3 — Attachment glyph is two-state.** `undefined` (unknown) and `false` both render nothing — inconsistent with the row's 3-state read marker (dot / hollow ring). Either an outline "unknown" paperclip or a documented convention.
- **P3 — From-searches drop date captions** (calendar orientation lost exactly where recency matters) + the "AND OR" help run-on.

Minor: no input placeholder (fresh session shows an empty suggestion box), unstyled native clear-X duplicates the header X, `maxlength=512` chars vs 512-byte grammar cap (now caught inline), near-duplicate `search-clear`/`context-back` exits.

**Trend for `ue-search-surface-vs-superhuman-search-screenshots` (last 5 runs): 27 → 34** — wrote `.impeccable/critique/2026-11-07T22-10-41Z__ue-search-surface-vs-superhuman-search-screenshots.md`. Evidence: `/private/tmp/email-os-search-critique2/` (screenshots 01–11, `evidence.txt`, `console-events.jsonl`, `detect.json`).

## Questions
1. **Auto-collapse on submit + clickable query header as the only edit path** (the P1+P2 pair, biggest remaining reference-parity win) — do it?
2. From-searches **lose date captions** — acceptable parity with the reference, or nest date captions under sender captions?
3. Scope: just those two, or also the listbox hardening (P2) and the glyph three-state (P3)?
Use subagents to implement solutions for the remaining issues

- **Syntax error** (`subject:`, critique3/06): peak = immediate specific alert `"subject:" needs a value — e.g. subject:"example".` while typing; if it reaches the provider, banner names `/` + header as reopen paths and hides dead Retry. **Good — the trust moment is handled.**
- **Grouped from-search** (fix2/05, critique3/10): peak = `Ada Fixture (15)` instantly says scale; end = nested "January 2025" keeps recency. Mild mid-scan friction: sender vs date captions look identical. **Positive with a nit.**
- **Edit via header**: click `Search: q` → form reopens focused, query seeded (fix2/02); end = resubmit collapses again. **Smooth**; nit = query shown twice while open.
- **Restore round trip** (reader → Back, or context-back): same query, rows, cursor, focus, collapsed state — "it remembered exactly." **Strongest trust beat.**

## 6. PRODUCT-SLOP verdict

**Yes — a Linear/Notion/Raycast-fluent user would now trust this.** Palette-vocabulary listbox with the lavender-bar highlight, query-as-header matching the reference, honest coverage that survives collapse, no dead Retry, three-state glyph consistent with the read marker, zero console errors, no overflow at 1440×900, all text ≥ AA in evidence. **New subtly-off details introduced by the backlog fixes:**
1. **Header button reads as static text at rest** — `.search-results-query` is a padding-0 ghost (`style.css:846`); only hover fill / `title` / aria-label reveal clickability. At rest it is indistinguishable from a heading.
2. **Auto-collapse vs open-form duplication** — while editing in search context the query appears twice (header + input).
3. **Caption nesting density** — sender and date captions share identical `.row-group` styling; each is a 48px block, so N senders × M date buckets = heavy caption spam in broad results (fixture hides this: 2 senders, 1 date bucket).
4. **Outline-glyph noise + contrast** — every legacy (pre-v4) cache row renders the outline paperclip; on a real mailbox that could be most rows. On focused rows the glyph is 2.75:1 (evidence CONTRAST), and ×0.75 opacity makes the unknown variant lower still; "outline = unknown" is only in title/aria, never on screen.
5. **Duplicate exits** — ← and X both = `contextBack`, plus the unstyled native ✕ (clears draft only) visible in fix2/02.
6. **Coverage line position when form open** — renders below the 8-line help, reads as form output (fine when collapsed).

## 7. STRENGTHS

1. **The search round trip is exact and tested end-to-end**: auto-collapse on submit with focus handoff to the first row, four reopen paths through one `revealSearch()`, stepped Esc, and restore that keeps query/rows/cursor/focus/collapsed-state (`app.search-form.component.test.ts:303`, `app.search-sender-groups.test.ts` restore tests).
2. **Honest state implemented literally (PRODUCT.md #1)**: inline grammar mirror with example-bearing errors gated before the provider, conditional banner copy that never points at a hidden form, Retry removed when it would re-fail identically, coverage line always mounted.
3. **Three-state attachment glyph wired end-to-end**: Rust `Option<bool>` never inferred (`mail-core/src/search.rs:169-186`) → schema v4 wire field → `RowGlyph` solid/outline/none → DESIGN.md:316 documents it — unknown is never rendered as silence, matching the 3-state read marker.

## 8. PRIORITY ISSUES (remaining)

- **P1 — Triple exit + unstyled native clear-X.** `data-test="context-back"` (`App.vue:1962`) and `data-test="search-clear"` (`App.vue:2097`) both call `contextBack()`; the native `type="search"` ✕ appears whenever the draft is non-empty, is unstyled, and only clears text — three exits, two semantics, one dead-looking control (PRODUCT.md anti-reference). *Fix:* style or hide `::-webkit-search-cancel-button`; keep one visible exit in search context (the results-header X) and let ← keep generic Back semantics. → `/impeccable distill` + `harden` on the search results header.
